target_audience: University students (Teacher Education or STEM majors)

sections.title: Introduction: The Goal of Mathematical Clarity
lecture_lines: Mathematical clarity bridges the gap to understanding.
Correctness alone is not enough for accessibility.
An explanation needs a clear path and legend.
animations: Fade in title '#FFFFFF' text 'Mathematical Clarity' center.
Highlight title with '#FFFF00' color for emphasis.
Appear definition: 'Clarity is bridging knowledge gaps'. Color '#00FF00'.

sections.title: Criterion 1: Scaffolding and Prerequisite Alignment
lecture_lines: Activate prior knowledge before complex concepts.
Use visual layering to build foundations.
Example: Nested gears visualize function composition.
animations: Fade in text 'Scaffolding' color '#FFFFFF' left side.
Fade in line connecting Scaffolding to 'Prerequisites'. Color '#FFFFFF'.

sections.title: Criterion 2: The Power of Multi-Representational Fluency
lecture_lines: Fluency requires moving between different representations.
Algebra, verbal, and graphical forms work together.
Visual-spatial reasoning reduces abstract cognitive load.
Example: Pythagorean theorem water flow animation.
Geometry transitions smoothly into symbolic algebra.
animations: Fade in graph labeled 'Concept A' color '#00FFFF'.
Fade in equation labeled 'Formula B' color '#FF00FF'.
Show arrow linking graph and equation with color '#FFFFFF'.
Pulse both elements to show interconnectedness, color '#FFFF00'.

sections.title: Criterion 3: Precision vs. Intuition (The 'Just-in-Time' Rule)
lecture_lines: Establish the hook before high-level formalism.
Use scenarios to anchor abstract principles.
Example: Robot path choosing in labyrinths.
Total sample space precedes odd calculation.
animations: Animate scale of Intuition, color '#FF8000', over Precision.

sections.title: Conclusion: Reflection and Self-Check
lecture_lines: Effective testing means the student can re-teach.
Use the Clarity Compass to audit presentations.
